So last week I started eating as strict of a keto diet as I can manage, managing to stay below 25g net carbs for the most part (today's salad pushed me up to about 30). I cut out all the tasty starchy and sugary foods and started eating a lot more meat and veggies. The weight's starting to come off, but there's just one big issue: I have never been so consistently hungry in my life. Before, a peanut butter and jelly sandwich and a glass of milk would hold me over for 12 hours. Now, I can grill up a chicken breast or a steak and then fry up some veggies until my plate is mounded with food, have three glasses of water, and an hour later I'm back in the kitchen opening up a can of tuna.

Is this a normal reaction and does it go away?

How much fat are you eating? Are you tracking calories and macros? It sounds to me like you're not eating enough. Personally, I recommend people try not to eat at a deficit for the first couple weeks. Your body is already going to be dealing with changing to a new fuel source and that adaptation. It only adds more stress to try and do that at a calorie deficit. Most people ignore that advice and do it at a deficit anyway. They survive. But, the start would have been significantly less miserable if they ate until they couldn't stand to eat any more.

It is normal if you're not eating enough fat, protein, or calories. It does go away. The keto diet is well known for how it reduces feelings of hunger and makes losing weight pretty easy and pain-free.

I'm tracking what I eat as best I can, and so far I'm averaging about 1800 calories a day, which is probably more than I was eating before. Fat intake bounces around a little more, but I seem to be averaging about 100g per day so far. I'm relieved to hear it's normal at the start. Eating well is surprisingly more expensive than eating crap all the time. I'm going to go have some more tuna. I'm just happy my mayo doesn't have any carbs in it.

If you're eating 100g of fat, 25g of carbs, and hitting 1800 calories a day then you're probably over-doing the protein. That is like 200g of protein a day. Why not find fattier sources? Chicken breast and tuna is pretty lean, although you mentioned mayo for the tuna which helps.

I'd try and exchange some of that protein for fat. Keep eating as much as you want for the first couple weeks. Your hunger should go away, and you'll feel better. It gets a lot easier.
